title: 7th-inning single completes cycle for Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong
content:
CHICAGO — While dealing with a lineup-wide slump, Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell only has so many cards to play. Prospects can be called up from Triple A, with hopes of providing new energy. An established player on a long-term contract can get benched for a “mental reset.” Reshuffling the order always sounds good, but it only works if the hitters actually produce.

Leading off with Pete Crow-Armstrong certainly appears to be an inspired idea, even if, ideally, he would bring the same level of focus to every game situation. And the Cubs only get so much credit for having to do something amid this offensive spiral.

But, yes, Crow-Armstrong is again looking like a superstar.

Crow-Armstrong hit for the cycle during Monday’s game against the Colorado Rockies, putting on a show for the crowd of 38,337 on a postcard 76-degree night at Wrigley Field.

“Look, I told him this: ‘There is a responsibility of hitting first in a lineup,’” Counsell said recently. “We are choosing you to hit the most. I mean, that’s how baseball works, right? So that’s a responsibility. Hopefully, that means something. We still want every at-bat to mean something, too. And every at-bat is important, and every moment is important. But if that works for him, that would be helpful.”

The loud crack of the bat echoed throughout the ballpark when Crow-Armstrong launched Michael Lorenzen’s fourth pitch of the game 434 feet into the center-field bleachers.

In the third inning, Crow-Armstrong drilled another Lorenzen pitch off the wall in right-center field, racing for a triple. He notched a double off Lorenzen in the fifth inning by driving a ball into the right-field corner, moving closer toward a historic performance.

Shortly after singing “Take Me Out To The Ball Game,” the crowd chanted “P-C-A! P-C-A!” Crow-Armstrong lined a single off lefty reliever Brennan Bernardino into right field to complete the 13th cycle in franchise history.

And then, underlining how inconsistent the Cubs have been this season, Crow-Armstrong got picked off at first base.

The last Cub to hit for the cycle was Carson Kelly, who did it on March 31 last year against the Athletics. Crow-Armstrong is only the second Cubs center fielder since 1901 to hit for the cycle, joining Hall of Famer Hack Wilson, who turned the feat on June 23, 1930.
